messages:
sam: Quick async check — trying to finalize the API contract for the model chooser param before I open the PR. Question: how should the runtime resolve model selection when clients pass both a legacy `model` string and the new `model_ids` array plus optional `routing_hints`? Need to be explicit about fallback order and response shape so SDKs don't break.

sam: example payload we're seeing from a few clients:
```json
{
  "model": "redwood-13b",       // legacy single-model param
  "model_ids": ["rw-13b-highmem", "rw-13b-quant"],
  "routing_hints": {"region": "eu", "tier": "dedicated"}
}
```

sam: Expected resolution behavior I think makes sense: prefer explicit `model_ids` order (first element primary), apply routing_hints to pick region/tier compatible variant, if none available fall back to legacy `model`, then global fallback chain. But want confirmation that this is the agreed contract and what the runtime will put in the response `served_model` field.

mira: Agree with preferring `model_ids` order. Implementation notes: runtime should treat `model` as a single-element fallback (older clients) only if `model_ids` is absent or empty. If both present, `model_ids` takes precedence. Routing hints are soft preferences — we try to honor region/tier but will return next compatible variant if strict match not available. I'll add exact bullet points in the PR. :+1:

jonah: Quick concern on response shape: current clients parse `served_model.id` and `served_model.variant_tier`. If we start returning an array (multiple attempted candidates) that will break them. Suggest we keep `served_model` as an object with these fields: `id`, `variant`, `region`, `resolved_from` (values: "model_ids", "model", "fallback"). If we want to expose the candidate list add `served_model_candidates` optional array (new field) so old clients keep working.

mira: +1 to jonah. Keep `served_model` stable. `served_model_candidates` can be present only when `include_debug` flag is set (or when request has `debug=true`) so we don't change normal responses.

sam: sounds good. Also, confirm that `model_ids` ordering is authoritative (we won't reorder based on region preference) — we should only skip an entry when it's incompatible and move to the next.

mira: Correct. Ordering is authoritative. The runtime will not reorder `model_ids` for preference; it will filter out incompatible ones then pick first compatible in order. If none are compatible, fallback to `model` if present, then to system fallback.

jonah: One more edge case: what if `model_ids` contains variants that exist only in us-west but routing_hints say `region: eu` — do we treat them as incompatible or as viable via cross-region routing (higher latency/cost)? We need to encode that policy.

mira: Good point. Policy: by default routing_hints are hard for region (i.e., incompatible == cannot serve) for customers with `region_enforcement=true` (enterprise). For general accounts we allow cross-region if `allow_cross_region` is true in the account settings; otherwise it's incompatible. We'll document default (allow_cross_region=false).

sam: Great. Can someone confirm the exact `served_model` JSON example we'll return so SDKs can be updated?

jonah: Proposed minimal stable shape:
```json
"served_model": {
  "id": "rw-13b-highmem",
  "variant": "highmem",
  "region": "us-west-2",
  "resolved_from": "model_ids"
}
```
And optional debug array: `served_model_candidates: [ {id, variant, region, reason} ]` when debug=true.

mira: That matches my view. Also add `resolved_reason` codes we can use in telemetry: `selected`, `skipped_incompatible`, `fallback_model_param`, `global_fallback` etc.

infra-bot: Reminder: there's an open design doc draft at https://go/redwood/model-chooser-spec (internal) — CI lint for API schema will run once PR opened.

tess: I'll volunteer to review the SDK change. Ping me when PR is up.

sam: Thanks all — I'll open the small contract PR with bullets: precedence rules, response shape (served_model + optional candidates), routing enforcement flags, and add unit tests. CC @mira @jonah @tess for review. Expecting to link the PR here in ~1h.

mira: Thanks — if anyone has objections post them here, otherwise we'll merge once tests and API lint pass.

tess: :thumbsup:
